extracted.intended_audience: IP researchers, statisticians, policymakers, and IP office staff who use or interpret WIPO design and plant-variety statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and methodological notes for reading and comparing WIPO design (and related IP) statistical tables and charts, including definitions, scope, and cautions about comparability and completeness. Intended to help analysts correctly interpret counts, rates, and procedural metrics across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability across offices
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO collects data from offices using a common questionnaire and methodology. However, because of differences in design procedures between offices, data cannot be fully harmonized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, caution should be exercised when making comparisons across offices. Procedural differences (e.g., substantive vs formal examination, reporting conventions) can affect metrics such as registrations, rejections, pendency and examiner counts; direct office-to-office comparisons may be misleading without adjusting for procedural differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — registrations in force vs designs contained
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to the number of design registrations in force and not the number of designs contained within those registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should not treat 'registrations in force' as equivalent to the raw count of individual designs; a single registration may cover one or multiple designs depending on office practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of WIPO estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO estimates cover 139 IP offices and include direct national and regional applications, as well as designations received via the Hague System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported totals and growth rates reflect this combined coverage; users should note whether figures include Hague designations or only direct filings when conducting further analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design protection duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Design rights generally last for up to 15 years from the filing date. In China that protection period is limited to 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing age distributions or 'in force' cohorts, adjust expectations and calculations for jurisdictions with shorter maximum protection periods (e.g., China).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of registration-year persistence percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages are calculated using the number of designs registered in year t and in force in 2024 divided by the total number of designs registered in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the denominator and numerator for the plotted persistence metric; replicating the measure requires applying the same year‑t registration cohort and checking in‑force status in 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph/sample selection for year-by-year breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: The graph is based on data from 92 offices (including most of the larger offices) for which a breakdown of design registrations in force by year of registration was available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts using this breakdown are limited to offices that reported the necessary time-series detail; absence of an office from the graph may be due to missing breakdown data rather than zero activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency classification for regional offices
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed at a regional office is considered to be a resident filing, if the applicant resides in one of that office’s member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying filings by origin, treat regional-office filings as 'resident' only when the applicant's residence is within the region's member states; this affects resident/non-resident splits for regional offices (e.g., EUIPO, OAPI, Benelux).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete origin data (design count by origin)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design count by origin data are incomplete, because some offices do not report the relevant data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses by origin may undercount or be biased; users should check office-level reporting completeness before drawing conclusions about geographic origin distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hague designation / origin reporting caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Only Hague designation data are available and/or this office has not reported the origin of applications therefore the design count by office and origin data may be incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where only Hague designation information exists (or where offices omit origin), origin-based aggregates and resident/abroad splits should be treated as partial and potentially non-comparable across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation legend
rubrics_metrics.description: n.a. indicates not applicable. .. indicates not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect these annotations when parsing tables; do not interpret 'n.a.' or '..' as numeric zeros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural data harmonization caveat (procedural metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO collects procedural data from offices using a common questionnaire and methodology. Every effort has been made to compile procedural data based on common definitions and concepts, but procedural differences make it extremely difficult to fully harmonize such data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution should therefore be exercised when making comparisons across offices for procedural indicators (e.g., distribution of examination outcomes, first office action times, final decision times, number of examiners). Differences in procedural definitions, phases counted, and reporting practices can materially affect these metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete application-processing totals
rubrics_metrics.description: The total number of applications processed for any given office may be incomplete due to the omission of one or several elements by the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate 'applications processed' figures should be interpreted with care; missing components from office submissions can produce undercounts in the published totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTE definition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the FTE definition when comparing examiner counts; reported numbers represent equivalent full-time staff rather than headcount if some staff are part-time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of dominant contributors from specific charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Because China accounts for most of the global total, it is excluded from this graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some charts deliberately exclude dominant offices to reveal patterns among smaller offices; verify whether an exclusion was applied before comparing charted values to global totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office naming and country-formal-name clarifications
rubrics_metrics.description: EUIPO is the European Union Intellectual Property Office. Note: Iran is the Islamic Republic of Iran. Netherlands is the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize standardized or formal naming conventions used in tables and notes to avoid confusion when matching offices/countries to external datasets.
